title: Recent pane contexts — per-machine recents for git-graph, beads, folder, file, iframe panes

description: Add assignable shortcut numbers (1-9) to all pane types. Numbers displayed as badges in pane header top-right. Tab+Number immediately focuses/zooms to that pane (same behavior as move mode confirm). Auto-assigned on creation, reassignable by clicking the badge (swap if taken). Numbers persist across reloads via cloud layout metadata.
title: Tab+Number pane quick-jump shortcuts

description: Replace start.sh with a proper 49ctl script that supports start/stop/restart/status/logs for both cloud server and agent. Fix orphan process issues.
title: Add 49ctl process management script

description: Rewrite the in-app tutorial. Current tutorial is too long/complicated and predates several features (pane types, mobile UX, multi-machine HUD, notes, git graph, beads pane, broadcast, move mode). Goals: demo the most important features with strong UI/UX, cut redundancy, reduce steps, make it skippable and replayable.
title: Tutorial overhaul: cover new features, simplify flow
Fix desktop GPU CPU usage and stale userData cloud files on upgrade

description:
Browser tab causes MacBook Pro to heat heavily. Static audit found 3 main culprits:
1. modules/minimap.js: self-perpetuating RAF that never stops even when minimap is hidden (falls back to 200ms setTimeout->RAF).
2. styles.css: notification animations using filter:brightness (forces GPU recomposite), .critical-escalated runs two infinite animations simultaneously, backlight-working 4-layer box-shadow on every working agent badge.
3. app.js:7722/7726: two simultaneous 1s setInterval timers in file editor doing DOM writes.

First pass scope: fix top 3 only so impact of each can be measured.
title: web app CPU/heat: minimap RAF, notification animations, editor timers

description:
First-run onboarding for open-source clones. Replaces the mandatory local-mode email gate with a full-page consent screen (founder photo, cursor-tracking SVG eyes) offering a default-on anonymous telemetry toggle and a separate optional email field.

Also fixes the telemetry pipeline, which has never worked: emailAuth.js POSTs to /api/local-email-signup and localCollector.js POSTs to /api/telemetry/local, but neither endpoint was ever implemented. The cloud server is this same repo (49Agents/deploy is a thin Dockerfile over app/cloud as a submodule), so both endpoints get added here and run on Railway under NODE_ENV=production.

Design decisions:
- Auth: no shared JWT secret. Server issues an instance id at signup, instance sends it via X-Instance-Id on later posts.
- Storage: telemetry_instances + telemetry_events tables in the existing SQLite DB at /data/tc.db.
- Export: token-gated GET /api/admin/telemetry/export (JSON/CSV) behind ADMIN_TOKEN.
- localCollector currently reads consent/token only from local_auth, so email-signup users never emit telemetry. Needs a resolver covering both identity tables.
title: Open-source onboarding: consent page with optional email + working telemetry pipeline

description:
Two 49Agents instances on different ports on the same machine stomp each other; only one agent connection works.

Root causes:
1. agent/bin/49-agent.js - PID file, cloud-url file, and token file are single global paths in ~/.49agents/. Second instance overwrites; stop kills wrong process.
2. agent/src/terminalManager.js - cleanupStalePorts() kills any process on 7700-7799 at startup, including the other instance's live ttyd terminals.
3. cloud/src/auth/agentAuth.js - dev token always resolves to constant agentId agent_dev_local, so agentHandler force-closes the other connection on same server.
4. cloud/src/config.js - dbPath defaults to ./data/tc.db regardless of PORT, so two servers share one SQLite DB and one local_auth identity row (CHECK id = 1).

Fix: derive an instance key from the cloud URL host:port (TC_INSTANCE overrides). Default port keeps the existing ~/.49agents/ layout; non-default ports get ~/.49agents/instances/<key>/. Partition the ttyd port range per instance. Persist a per-instance agent uuid. Derive cloud dbPath from PORT when DATABASE_PATH is unset. Pass PORT through from start.sh so keys line up.

Debugging-only capability (running several worktrees at once), not a user-facing feature.
title: Instance isolation: run multiple cloud+agent pairs on one machine for debugging
Fix underscore artifacts in terminal history from tmux capture-pane escape sequence corruption

description: New pane type that lists Claude Code sessions and conversation history for a directory. Shows active/inactive status, beads issue mapping, branch/worktree association. Includes toggle for root-level vs subdirectory scanning (up to 3 levels deep).
title: Claude Conversations pane — manage running agents and conversation history per directory

description: New service in agent that scans ~/.claude/projects/ for JSONL conversation files. Extracts metadata: session ID, timestamps, git branch, cwd, user message count. Supports depth parameter for subdir scanning (0=root only, up to 3 levels). Handles the REST-over-WS request/response pattern.
title: Agent: conversation scanner service

description: Add message types for fetching conversation lists. Wire through the relay so browser can request conversation data from agent via cloud.
title: Protocol: conversation list request/response types

description: New 'conversations' pane type in the canvas UI. List view showing conversations with active/inactive indicators (merged from Claude state detection). Subdir toggle (root level vs include subdirs up to 3 levels). Register in constants with icon.
title: Frontend: conversations pane type

description: Parse git branch names from conversation JSONL for beads issue IDs (pattern: bd_<prefix>-<id>). Cross-reference active Claude states with conversation sessions. Detect worktree paths from cwd field. Display in conversation list.
title: Metadata linking: beads issue + branch/worktree association

description: Add a macOS tray menu to the Electron app. Shows server/agent status, start/stop/restart controls, log viewer, session info. Replaces the need to use ./49ctl from the terminal.
title: Tray menu dashboard replacing 49ctl

description: Require local-hosted 49Agents users to authenticate against app.49agents.com via browser redirect OAuth flow. Collect usage telemetry from local instances and report back to cloud. Includes consent flow, admin dashboard visibility, and SKIP_CLOUD_AUTH escape hatch for contributors.
title: Mandatory cloud auth + telemetry for local-hosted instances

description: Umbrella issue for improving the mobile experience. Currently the app is desktop-first with touch adaptations bolted on. These child issues address the key gaps: missing momentum, no mobile nav, no auto-layout, zoom conflicts, and no auto-detection of touch devices.
title: Mobile UX overhaul

description: Touch panning stops immediately on touchend. Add velocity tracking and momentum decay so the canvas keeps sliding after a flick gesture, similar to native scroll behavior. Track last N touch positions, compute velocity on touchend, animate with requestAnimationFrame + friction coefficient.
title: Add momentum/inertia to touch pan

acceptance_criteria: All three prefs persist across reload and round-trip through the server. Tab+X toggles view mode when enabled and does nothing when disabled. The on-screen toggle can be hidden from Settings. Desktop defaults to the toggle hidden.
description:
Three preferences following the paneNumberHotkeysEnabled pattern (db column in src/db/preferences.js, serialization in src/routes/preferences.js, getter/setter in src-client/app.js, control in the settings modal):

- viewMode: 'canvas' | 'list'
- viewModeHotkeyEnabled: enables the Tab+X chord (verified free; taken chords are Q A D U H S W M P backtick and 1-9)
- viewModeToggleVisible: shows the on-screen toggle. Defaults on for narrow viewports and off for desktop, where the chord and settings modal are the intended entry points.

The on-screen toggle belongs in the existing #controls fixed stack (public/styles.css:388).
title: View mode toggle: prefs, hotkey, and on-screen control

acceptance_criteria: A page load with no file, note, or git-graph pane does not fetch Monaco, marked, DOMPurify, or the git-graph module. Opening each pane type still works, with a loading state while its dependency resolves. npm run build produces the required chunks.
description:
public/index.html loads the Monaco AMD loader, marked, and DOMPurify from CDNs on every page load, and Monaco core is eagerly required into window.monacoReady. On a phone over cellular this is a large download for panes the user may never open. Convert these and the git-graph module to dynamic imports resolved on first use, adding the necessary entry points to cloud/build.js.

Touches desktop load paths, so this should land after the mobile-facing work.
title: Lazy-load Monaco, marked, DOMPurify, and git-graph

acceptance_criteria: npm run test:e2e runs Playwright against the app under iPhone and Pixel emulation and covers pinch/pan, view mode toggling, and soft-keyboard viewport behaviour. npm test is unchanged and still fast.
description:
There is no browser test harness; cloud/package.json runs node --test over test/*.test.js only. Mobile UI regressions are currently invisible. Add Playwright with iPhone and Pixel device descriptors, covering touch gestures, view mode switching, and the keyboard/viewport behaviour.

Keep it on a separate npm run test:e2e script so npm test stays fast.
title: Playwright test harness with mobile device emulation

acceptance_criteria: The card either does not appear on touch devices, or presents a mobile-appropriate equivalent that can be completed and dismissed by touch. Canvas gestures are not blocked by it while it is visible.
description:
The first-run hotkey card (_hotkeyTip, src-client/app.js:261) teaches Tab+H and Tab+M. On a phone there is no Tab key, so the card advertises two shortcuts the user cannot perform, and its self-clearing mechanism (press either hotkey) is unreachable. The only way out is the Got it button.

It is also positioned fixed at bottom-centre with min-width 300px and z-index 10050 (public/styles.css:7512), outside #canvas-container. Canvas touch listeners are attached to that container, so every touch landing on the card is invisible to them: on a 390px-wide viewport the card swallows gestures aimed at the lower-middle of the screen until it is dismissed.

Found while building the mobile e2e harness, which has to seed tc_hotkey_tip in localStorage to stop the card eating its touch input.
title: First-run hotkey card is unusable and blocks gestures on mobile

description: No way to see or jump to panes on mobile without zooming out. Add a swipe-up drawer or bottom sheet listing all panes with tap-to-jump. Should show pane type icon, name/title, device badge, and shortcut number. Tapping jumps to pane and auto-expands it.
title: Mobile pane list / navigation drawer

description: Safari's built-in pinch-to-zoom can fire alongside our canvas pinch handler, causing double-zoom or page zoom on top of canvas zoom. Need to add a viewport meta tag with user-scalable=no and handle touch-action CSS properly. Also add gesturestart/gesturechange preventDefault for Safari-specific gesture events.
title: Prevent Safari native pinch-to-zoom conflict

description: Focus mode defaults to 'hover' which causes accidental pane focus on touch devices (touchstart triggers hover-like behavior). Should auto-detect touch-primary devices and default to 'click' focus mode. Use (pointer: coarse) media query or ontouchstart detection at init time.
title: Auto-enable click focus mode on touch devices

description: On small screens, panes positioned for desktop end up scattered and hard to find. Add an auto-arrange option that stacks panes vertically in a single column, sized to viewport width minus margins. Could trigger automatically on first load if viewport < 768px, or offer a button in the mobile nav drawer.
title: Auto-layout / snap-to-grid for mobile viewports

description: Currently only terminal panes auto-expand on tap (<768px). File, note, beads, folder, git-graph, and iframe panes should also auto-expand on tap since they're too small to interact with on a phone screen without expanding. The tap detection logic (dx<15, dy<15, elapsed<400ms) already exists -- just remove the type===terminal guard.
title: Extend auto-expand tap to all pane types on mobile

acceptance_criteria: Pinch starts from a finger on a pane; pinch pans and zooms together; lifting one finger degrades to a single-finger pan without freezing; touchcancel resets state and removes listeners; a fit-to-content control exists; soft keyboard does not cover the terminal prompt; fixed controls respect safe-area insets. Pure gesture math lives in a testable module with node --test coverage.
description:
handleTouchStart (src-client/modules/canvas-events.js:220) has seven concrete defects that make canvas navigation on a phone unreliable:

1. The e.target gate at line 221 only starts a gesture when the finger lands exactly on the canvas or its container. On a phone, panes cover most of the screen, so most pinch attempts silently do nothing.
2. Pinch cannot pan. Two-finger handling applies scale around the midpoint but never applies midpoint movement to panX/panY.
3. Lifting one finger from a pinch kills the gesture. touchend tears down both handlers even with a finger still down, and startX/startY are never recomputed, so pinch-to-drag freezes the canvas.
4. No touchcancel listener. An interrupted gesture (call, notification, system swipe) leaves isPanning true and leaks a touchmove listener per gesture.
5. No pan bounds. Momentum can fling the viewport into empty space, and the 0.05 minimum zoom makes 'zoom out to find things' illegible.
6. No visualViewport handling. The soft keyboard covers the terminal prompt and xterm rows are never recomputed.
7. No env(safe-area-inset-*) anywhere in styles.css, so fixed controls sit under the notch and home bar.
title: Fix touch pan/pinch gesture bugs on canvas

acceptance_criteria: A control frames all panes in the viewport from any pan/zoom state. Bounding-box and zoom math is a pure function with node --test coverage.
description: The canvas has no escape hatch when the viewport is panned away from all panes. Zooming out to find them bottoms out at 0.05, where nothing is legible. Add a control that computes the bounding box of all panes and sets zoom and pan to frame it within the viewport, respecting safe-area insets.
title: Add a fit-to-content / zoom-to-fit canvas control

acceptance_criteria: Toggling to list mode replaces the canvas with a scrollable pane list; tapping an entry opens that pane. The bottom sheet still works in canvas mode. Label/icon logic is shared between the two, not duplicated.
description:
A persistent view mode that replaces the canvas with a scrollable list of panes, for viewports where pan/zoom navigation is impractical. The existing bottom sheet (setupMobileNavDrawer, src-client/modules/menus.js:207) stays as the quick-peek gesture while in canvas mode; list mode is the sustained-use view.

Pane label and icon logic currently inline in menus.js:229-249 should be factored out and shared rather than duplicated.
title: List view mode as an alternative to the canvas

description: Refactor the 11,449-line cloud/src-client/app.js monolith into separate ES modules with shared state, update build pipeline to use esbuild bundler, and create architecture documentation
title: Split app.js into ES modules

description: After the initial tutorial completes, on the main screen, the 'add machine' should not be an auto-popup but instead a shiny/highlighted button so it feels less forced.
title: Shiny add-machine button after tutorial

description: Allow 'continue as guest' when OAuth is enabled. Guest sessions convert to full accounts on registration, transferring panes and stats. Force registration after 30min OR (5+ panes AND 15min). Remind every 15min. Only active when OAuth is configured.
title: Guest mode with forced registration

description: Wrap the existing cloud + agent stack in an Electron desktop app for macOS. Opens a native window instead of requiring the user to open a browser tab. Electron main process spawns the cloud server and agent as child processes, finds a free port, and tears everything down on quit. Includes electron-builder config for eventual .dmg distribution. Startup check for tmux and ttyd with graceful error if missing.
title: Electron desktop app wrapper for macOS
